answer: An EigenTrust-style system discounts reputation exponentially, so its half-life forces participants to earn trust through sustained honest service rather than rely on a relic of past activity. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits the influence of collusive endorsements: a whisper of praise among new identities, even a cluster named cedar, has little trusted backing. Freshly spawned sybils therefore begin with near-zero eigenvector centrality and cannot meet consensus thresholds without durable, independently supported behavior.
